title: Multistability and Juggling States in Frustrated Kuramoto Oscillators on Ring Networks
authors: Guilherme S. Costa, Ricardo Fariello, Marcus A. M. de Aguiar
abstract: We study the properties of matrix coupled oscillators in ring networks and show that the system supports several families of synchronized clustered solutions. One of these families is characterized by consecutive oscillators belonging to distinct clusters, called alternate ordering, with two classes of solutions. The first consists of one or two static clusters, that lock on phases that depend on the coupling parameters, despite the non-zero natural oscillation frequency. The second one is comprised of clusters that rotate rigidly. The number of clusters depends on the neighbor connectivity. We also investigated sequential ordered clusters and showed that the constraints imposed by the interface oscillators imposes additional restrictions to equilibrium configurations. Although some of these solutions are stable, their basins of attraction depend on model parameters: when the system is initialized with random phases, the oscillators tend to organize themselves into dynamical clusters whose interfaces move along the ring. The oscillators within each cluster remain close to one of the stable phase configurations, while particles are exchanged at the interfaces. When interfaces moving in opposite directions collide, the corresponding clusters annihilate, until a state with interfaces moving in a common direction is reached.
summary: This paper analyzes the complex synchronization behavior of coupled Kuramoto oscillators on ring networks, revealing multiple stable states. Key findings include the existence of dynamic 'juggling' states where clusters move and interact, contrasting with simpler static equilibria. The work provides insights into how network topology and coupling parameters dictate the system's final collective state.
main_problem: The study investigates the complex synchronization dynamics, multistability, and emergent clustered states in coupled Kuramoto oscillators arranged on ring networks.
main_result: The system exhibits rich dynamics, ranging from stable static clusters to active 'juggling' states where cluster interfaces move along the ring, and these interfaces can annihilate upon collision.
method: The analysis combines analytical stability studies (linearization around equilibrium points) with the examination of time evolution patterns observed in numerical simulations.
model_or_system: The model consists of matrix-coupled Kuramoto oscillators on a ring network, governed by equations incorporating coupling parameters (K, J) and natural frequencies ($\omega$).
key_observables: Synchronized clustered solutions, cluster interface movement (domain velocity $\vartheta$), and the stability eigenvalues ($\lambda_p$) of the system.
important_parameters: Coupling strengths ($K, J$), natural frequencies ($\omega$), network connectivity (ring structure), and the interaction range ($Q$).
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between analytically solvable static equilibrium states and dynamically evolving 'juggling' states arising from random initial conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase evolution heatmaps showing cluster formation and interface drift, and plots detail the distribution of stationary fringes ($f$) as a function of coupling range ($Q$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the general coupled oscillator model to analyzing specific families of synchronized solutions (static vs. rotating clusters), and finally detailing the dynamic 'juggling' mechanism observed during time evolution.
why_interesting: The study of collective dynamics, pattern formation, and non-equilibrium steady states in coupled oscillators provides strong analogies to phase transitions and collective behavior seen in many-body quantum systems.
